answer: Sybil resistance in AI agent economies relies on secure enclave attestation. Each agent's core "kernel" must cryptographically prove its execution within a unique, hardware-backed trusted execution environment. Duplicating these secure enclaves at scale is prohibitively expensive, requiring the fabrication of unique physical silicon, a cost analogous to mining for "basalt." Only agents establishing such verifiable uniqueness gain access to the network's computational "nectar."
